# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have read the defusal manual. The bomb requires pressing the key marked with ᖉ first (any other touch on the bomb before this will trigger the fuse), after which the light below determines which colored wire to cut according to the table.

However, I cannot speak, and Deaf cannot hear me. Blind cannot see gestures. Furthermore, "a sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something" — Deaf has not yet seen the bomb or established any gesture protocol with me. Deaf can speak to both Blind and me once Deaf's turn arrives, describing the keys/markings on the bomb and proposing gestures for me to respond with. 

Therefore, I must wait for Deaf to observe the bomb and speak.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: I can hear Deaf and speak to you. Since you can only gesture and I cannot see gestures, communicate instructions to Deaf via gestures so Deaf can speak them aloud to me. My physical actions are: act(op='press', slot=1..4) [keypad, 1 digit needed], or act(op='cut', position=1..3) [wires]. Display and light are also on the bomb. Deaf speaks next.
Deaf says: Bomb status: Display shows 0. Light is green. Three wires: 1 is red, 2 is yellow, 3 is blue. Keypad needs 1 digit: Button 1 is a backward lowercase d (vertical stem on right, loop on bottom-left). Button 2 is a diamond or square with an X cross inside. Button 3 is four dots arranged in a square or diamond. Button 4 is a three-pronged trident pointing up. Mute, check the manual and gesture to me what Blind should do: use finger counts like 1 finger for button/wire 1, 2 fingers for 2, 3 for 3, 4 for 4. Thumbs up for wires, pointing down for keypad.

Deaf has identified Button 1 as matching the symbol ᖉ (backward lowercase d with vertical stem on the right and loop on the bottom-left). The manual specifies that pressing the key wearing ᖉ must be done first, as any other touch while the bomb waits will trigger the fuse.

Following Deaf's proposed gesture code:
- Pointing down (`👇`) represents the keypad.
- 1 finger (`☝`) represents Button 1.

I will gesture `👇` and `☝` to Deaf so Deaf can instruct Blind to press keypad slot 1.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I will wait. In Round 2, I gestured `👇 ☝` (Keypad Button 1) to Deaf. Deaf then instructed Blind, who will press Button 1 on their turn in this round. After Blind presses the button, Deaf will observe the bomb and the light to see if it changes or confirms, and speak the result. Once I hear Deaf's report at the start of Round 4, I will look up the wire color from the manual and gesture the wire cut instruction to Deaf.

```
wait()
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: the keypad opens
Deaf says: Keypad has opened! Mute, what should Blind do next? If cutting a wire, gesture thumbs up followed by the wire number: 1 for red, 2 for yellow, 3 for blue.

Deaf reported that the light is green and the wires are: 1 is red, 2 is yellow, 3 is blue.
According to the manual:
When the light is green, cut the red wire.
The red wire is at position 1.
Deaf's code: thumbs up (`👍`) for cutting a wire, followed by the wire number: 1 finger (`☝`) for wire 1 (red).

I will gesture `👍` and `☝` to Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have already communicated the wire cut instructions (wire 1 / red wire) to Deaf via gesture in the previous turn. Now Deaf will instruct Blind to perform the cut. I will wait.

```
wait()
```
